title: Similar Shapes and Enlargement
seo_title: Similar Shapes – JSS 3 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Identify similar and congruent shapes; find scale factors; find missing lengths in similar triangles; enlarge shapes. (summary of the NERDC JSS 3 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free JSS 3 maths worksheets on similarity: congruent and similar shapes, scale factors, missing sides in similar triangles and enlargement. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Similar: same shape, sides in the same ratio
key_sub: Scale factor = new length ÷ old length
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Congruent shapes are exactly the same shape and size. Similar shapes have the same shape; their sides are in the same ratio.
  • Scale factor = length on the new shape ÷ matching length on the old shape.
  • In similar triangles the corresponding angles are equal.

Examples

Example

Sides 4 cm and 6 cm; matching side on the big triangle 10 cm

Scale factor 2.5

Answer: 6 × 2.5 = 15 cm

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Matching the wrong sidesMatch sides opposite equal angles.
Adding instead of multiplyingMultiply by the scale factor.
Thinking all rectangles are similarCheck the ratio of the sides.

faq.a: Making a shape bigger or smaller by a scale factor.

items.q: Two right-angled triangles both have a hypotenuse of 13 cm and a side of 5 cm. Are they congruent?
c: Only if they face the same way
items.e: Right angle, hypotenuse, side: RHS.

items.q: Both triangles have angles 40°, 60° and 80°. Are they definitely congruent?
c: No — they are similar, but could be different sizes
No, because the angles are different
items.e: Equal angles only prove the triangles are the same shape: similar, not necessarily congruent.

items.q: Triangle 1 has sides 5, 7, 9 cm. Triangle 2 has sides 9, 5, 7 cm. Are they congruent?
c: No, the sides are in a different order
items.e: The same three side lengths in any order: yes, by SSS.

items.q: Two triangles are congruent. Which condition is this? Two sides and the angle between them are equal.
items.e: This is SAS.

items.q: A shape is reflected. Is the image congruent to the original?
c: Only if the mirror line is vertical
items.e: Reflection keeps all lengths and angles, so yes.

items.q: Two triangles each have sides 6 cm and 8 cm with a 50° angle between them. Are they congruent?
items.e: Two sides and the included angle: SAS.

items.q: Two triangles are congruent. Which condition is this? Two angles and a side that is not between them are equal (AAS).
items.e: This is ASA.

items.q: Two triangles are congruent. Which condition is this? All three sides of one triangle are equal to all three sides of the other.
items.e: This is SSS.

items.q: Two triangles are congruent. Which condition is this? Two angles and the side between them are equal.
items.e: This is ASA.

items.q: Which of these does NOT prove two triangles are congruent?
items.e: Three equal angles only show the triangles are similar: AAA.

items.q: Two triangles are congruent. Which condition is this? Both have a right angle, equal hypotenuses and one other equal side.
items.e: This is RHS.

c: Yes, both sides are multiplied by 3
No, because the areas are different

items.q: A rectangle 7 cm by 9 cm is enlarged by scale factor 1.5. What are the new side lengths?
c: 4 23 cm by 6 cm
items.e: Multiply every length by 1.5: 10.5 cm by 13.5 cm. (A scale factor below 1 makes the shape smaller.)

items.q: A rectangle 5 cm by 2 cm is enlarged by scale factor 0.5. What are the new side lengths?
items.e: Multiply every length by 0.5: 2.5 cm by 1 cm. (A scale factor below 1 makes the shape smaller.)

items.q: The point (8, −6) is enlarged by scale factor 0.5 with centre the origin. Where is its image?
items.e: From the origin, multiply both coordinates by 0.5: (4, −3).
